noise_assumptions.notes: Own assumption: a mature superconducting-style device (1q 0.1 %, 2q 1 %, readout 2 %, T1 100 us, T2 80 us). These values do NOT enter the Task B benchmark, which always applies the organiser model (1q 1 %, 2q 5 %, readout 2 %). At the organiser's 5x worse two-qubit error the design goal is fewest two-qubit gates, so SWAP-free routing matters most.

design_rationale: Our PS-Q1 classifier is a 4-qubit circuit (RY encoding, trainable RY/RZ, a ring of 4 CX gates, parity read-out), so the processor must contain a 4-cycle; 'diamond-4 (ring + chord 0-2)' has 4 qubits and 5 two-way links and compiles our circuit with 0 routing SWAPs (compiled depth 6, 4 two-qubit gates; logical circuit has 4). It also contains a triangle, which the mandatory QFT-3 needs for its three controlled-phase gates: official QFT-3 result is depth 16, 9 two-qubit gates, 0 SWAPs and noisy fidelity 0.6775. Every link is listed in both directions because the benchmark reverses a one-way CX with extra Hadamards: on a triangle this costs +0.0404 noisy QFT-3 fidelity (0.6280 one-way vs 0.6684 two-way). The native gate set {rx,ry,rz,h,cx} contains the ry, rz and cx our circuit is built from, so trained rotations are not re-synthesised; across the candidate gate sets the noisy QFT-3 fidelity spans 0.6579 to 0.6775. More qubits and links did not help: our Phase-1 9-qubit processor B reaches 0.6268, so extra connectivity beyond what the workload uses is unused cost, not benefit.
